newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees higher Mexican oils, meals imports.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees higher Mexican oils, meals imports.

text.p: Mexican vegetable oil imports in 1997/98 (Oct/Sept) should exceed 900,000 tonnes after an estimated 860,000 tonnes in 1996/97, Oil World said.
The independent weekly publication cited low opening stocks and a two percent rise in domestic consumption which it said would outweigh attempts to boost domestic oil production.
In oilmeals, the country was forecast to import perhaps six percent more than the 340,000 tonnes estimated for 1996/97.
This was assuming the poultry sector would continue to expand and some recovery was seen in beef and pork production.
The imports should be mainly soymeal, rapeseed meal and sunmeal.
Mexico's domestic meal production would not rise much in the forthcoming season, perhaps to 3.1 million tonnes after 3.0 million seen in 1996/97, Oil World said.
Mexico's domestic oilseed output may fall again in 1997/98 after a decline in 1996/97 and may necessitate higher soybean imports to feed its expanding processing capacity, it also said.
It forecast likely soybean imports at up to three million tonnes in 1997/98 (Sept/Aug), representing a 10 percent increase over 1996/97.
